title: HTML Audio and Video
summary: Embed sound and video with the audio and video elements, offer several formats with source, add captions with track and embed hosted video responsibly.
introduction: Browsers play audio and video natively: no plug-ins, no third-party player required. The `<audio>` and `<video>` elements give you built-in controls, several formats for compatibility, poster images, captions and subtitles. This lesson covers the elements, the attributes that make media behave well (and the ones that annoy users), and how to embed video hosted on another site.
learningObjectives: Embed audio and video with native controls
Provide multiple sources, a poster and captions
Embed hosted video with an iframe safely

blocks.code:
<audio controls src="https://interactive-examples.mdn.mozilla.net/media/cc0-audio/t-rex-roar.mp3">
  Your browser does not support the audio element.
</audio>

blocks.content: <audio controls src="https://interactive-examples.mdn.mozilla.net/media/cc0-audio/t-rex-roar.mp3">Your browser does not support the audio element.</audio>

blocks.text: `controls` shows the play button, timeline and volume. Without it the audio is invisible and can only be started with JavaScript. The text inside the element is only shown by browsers that do not understand `<audio>` at all, which today means almost none.

blocks.code:
<video controls width="320" height="180" poster="https://placehold.co/320x180/0b1120/ffffff?text=Poster" preload="metadata">
  <source src="https://interactive-examples.mdn.mozilla.net/media/cc0-videos/flower.webm" type="video/webm">
  <source src="https://interactive-examples.mdn.mozilla.net/media/cc0-videos/flower.mp4" type="video/mp4">
  Your browser does not support the video element.
</video>

blocks.content: <video controls width="320" height="180" poster="https://placehold.co/320x180/0b1120/ffffff?text=Poster" preload="metadata"><source src="https://interactive-examples.mdn.mozilla.net/media/cc0-videos/flower.webm" type="video/webm"><source src="https://interactive-examples.mdn.mozilla.net/media/cc0-videos/flower.mp4" type="video/mp4">Your browser does not support the video element.</video>

rows: Reserve space so the page does not jump when the video loads
`none`, `metadata` or `auto`: how much to download before the user presses play
Start automatically. Browsers only allow it when `muted` is also set
Play inside the page on iPhones instead of going full screen

blocks.text: Instead of a single `src`, list several `<source>` elements. The browser plays the first one it supports and ignores the rest. Put the smallest, most modern format first (WebM or AV1) and MP4 (H.264) last as the universal fallback. The `type` attribute lets the browser decide without downloading anything.

An `autoplay` video with sound is blocked by every modern browser, and even when allowed it is one of the most disliked things on the web. If you need autoplay for a silent background clip, combine `autoplay muted loop playsinline`.

`<track>` attaches a WebVTT file with captions (for people who cannot hear the audio), subtitles (translations) or descriptions. Captions are not optional for professional content: they are required by accessibility law in many countries and they make video searchable.

blocks.code:
<video controls width="640" height="360">
  <source src="intro.mp4" type="video/mp4">
  <track kind="captions" src="intro-en.vtt" srclang="en" label="English" default>
  <track kind="subtitles" src="intro-es.vtt" srclang="es" label="Español">
</video>

blocks.text: Video hosted on YouTube, Vimeo and similar services is embedded with an `<iframe>`, which places another web page inside yours. Give it a `title` for screen readers, use the provider's privacy-enhanced domain where available, and keep it responsive with a wrapper and CSS `aspect-ratio`.

blocks.code:
<iframe
  src="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/VIDEO_ID"
  title="Course introduction video"
  width="560" height="315"
  allow="accelerometer; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture"
  allowfullscreen
  loading="lazy">
</iframe>

blocks.text: Each embedded player loads hundreds of kilobytes of script. On pages with several videos, show a thumbnail and only load the iframe when the user clicks play; this site does exactly that for its video blocks.

blocks.title: Accessibility checklist for media
blocks.text: Native `controls`, captions for video, a transcript for audio, no autoplay with sound, and never rely on colour or sound alone to convey information.
